stem: Why are medium-chain triglycerides (MCTs) often used in the nutritional management of children with fat malabsorption pathways?

options.text: They bypass the standard digestion process and enter the portal venous system directly.
They are reconstituted into chylomichrons more efficiently than long-chain triglycerides.
They stimulate the production of pancreatic lipase to aid in the digestion of other fats.
They travel exclusively through the lymphatic system to avoid liver metabolism.

explanation: MCTs are unique because they do not require the standard hydrolysis and chylomicron reconstitution process, allowing for direct absorption into the portal system.
rationale: Consider how these specific fats differ in their entry into the systemic circulation compared to standard dietary fats.

optionExplanations.A: MCTs are unique because they do not require the standard hydrolysis and chylomicron reconstitution process, allowing for direct absorption into the portal system.
optionExplanations.B: While efficient absorption is the goal, MCTs actually bypass the reconstitution into chylomichrons entirely.
optionExplanations.C: MCTs are used because they can be absorbed even when pancreatic lipase is insufficient, not because they stimulate its production.
optionExplanations.D: Standard long-chain fats travel through the lymphatics; MCTs are beneficial because they enter the portal venous system instead.

source.hint: Consider how these specific fats differ in their entry into the systemic circulation compared to standard dietary fats.
